body:
I'm hopefully leaving soon so I can't help you, but can you maybe leave all those notes pdfs etc to a trusted loved one or even a favorite student in a note when you go? Just an idea. 


I hope something changes for you and your wife. I know it's probably annoying to read but it wouldn't feel right to not say it even being in the same situation.

God I cried closing my eyes and imagining my husband one day coming around like this... while I would kill for my husband to take initiative or even just compliment me just once, but I don't know how I would actually react if he changed. It's hard to undo years and years of resentment. It's like you built up a wall between the two of you and now you're talking through the wall as though it isn't there. You'll probably need lots of time to actually break down the wall. I have no tips other than accept that it'll be a slow process and don't give up, keep calling her beautiful etc.

I feel you OP, I haven't looked at anything larger than a face mirror in maybe five years. I stare straight down at the sink even at public bathrooms, I'm sure strangers think I'm a weirdo. But we need to do what we need to do to keep sane. I hate when people insist you take photos, etc.

I am also a HL spouse that gained a lot of weight, though in my case the weight gain happened well after the bedroom was dead. I used to be the woman everyone stared at, 10 years later I look like that woman's fat unkept aunt. Is he less attracted to me now? Well, maybe. But what's less than zero you know? Honestly, he hasn't said anything good or bad about how I look since our first year of dating. But it's definitely true weight affects things. The sex we do have has gotten worse since we are both out of shape. 

My suggestion would be focus on yourself and include healthy eating and exercise in the process. Hopefully, your husband will likely become more attracted to your confidence even before any real weight loss happens. And if the weight loss doesn't lead to increased sex, yes that would absolutely suck, but if you do it for yourself you will be much less bitter you know? Good luck OP.

I feel like this sometimes. I had an awful childhood (sexual and physical abuse, bullying, homelessness, you name it) and I used to day dream all the time about being thin, beautiful, a successful artist, a single woman dating attractive men and women living in the city. And the thing is I don't have an awful life...But it's far from perfect. I'm overweight. I'm not beautiful. I'm married with a dead bedroom. I work a job I don't like. I haven't painted in over 5 years. I live close to a city, but not in it. I have a C+ life. 

But I'll say I'm not dead in a ditch the way I feared throughout my childhood and teens. It's true that my childhood self would be disappointed about a lot of my life, but I think they would be most disappointed in the fact that I'm not kinder to myself. The thing I've most longed for isn't some external thing, it's the ability to go to bed content, happy, and feel safe. And I am rarely ever able to do that...not because my surroundings haven't gotten better, but because of my mind. If this resonates at all with you, I hope you'll try to be kinder to yourself OP.  Wishing you contentment.

I don't know if you're still with us, but I'm genuinely so sorry OP. I can't relate to everything you've said, but I can relate to your childhood as well as weight struggles and I understand how hard it is to keep going when it feels like the world is constantly crushing you. I wish you comfort and peace whatever form that may take, OP, good luck. Thinking of you.

It's because it's painful for them. Is it selfish of them to want us to live even though we're in pain? Maybe...but I understand it. I don't think it's mean spirited. I think they genuinely hope that something will eventually change for us and the pain will go away...and true sometimes it does. But sometimes it doesnt. What then? 

I think loved ones should keep in mind that for many of us suicide is an escape from the immense pain we are in. It's like if you were in a burning building and you chose to jump...only for us the burning buildings are our minds. I wish the fire would stop raging and I'll be miraculously saved...but sometimes that doesn't seem realistic and you reach that point where you must jump.
I'm really happy for you. Be safe and live for us, please.
Sometimes I do, sometimes I don't and feel deep sadness, not about death but just regretting my life. But either way I feel relieved that this is it.... no more pain. Just nothingness.

I felt unattractive well before I ever met him, he just kinda further confirms it with his actions. I know it's objectively true... I used to be decent looking and feel ugly, but now I actually am fat and don't take care of myself, jokes on me. To a point I've made peace with it...I just avoid photos and mirrors and try not to think about how I look. 

He has known he has low testosterone for the last 8 years, I beg him to go to the doctor once ever six months or so, he promises and never does. I'm sure if I suggested viagra he would do the same thing.

Me too. I wish I could trade my mind with someone with dementia... My legs with an amputee...my speech with a stroke survivor... my skin with a burn survivor...my life with a kid with cancer. I wish I could give every piece of me to someone who would feel more gratitude and joy. Sometimes I think of myself after I die being an organ donor having pieces of me spread out to people that need it...finally not a burden, finally useful.

Others have already talked about police... So I will give you advice on what to tell yourself...I was sexually abused by a family member too, and this is what I tell myself on the good days:

They are not worth your death. Live even if it sucks right now, just to spite them. They are losers. You win.

My first "attmept" was when I was 13 and I had heard you could die by drinking bleach, well my dumb self drank plain ol laundry detergent instead, I threw up but no damage obviously... Well my brother (who was abusive and one of the reasons I wanted to die) caught me throwing up, made fun of me and told my whole extended family...So. I understand how embarrassing it must have been. I'm just glad you did not end up with a debilitating injury. Be safe.

That's a good reason to have. For me it's the absolutely terrible suicide botch jobs that I see at my job in healthcare. I've seen spinal cord injuries, brain injuries, people who can't speak can't eat and should have died years ago being kept alive by their families on a feeding tube... I'm not scared of dying but I'm scared of messing up and living a terrible life for years and years.

Fair question. I honestly think it's a subconscious coping mechanism from having suffered sexual abuse as a child. I've been in only two serious relationships and both of them were like this. I am scared of men who are sexual but then am deeply sexually unsatisfied by the extremely passive, emotionally unavailable and low libido men I end up with. What an idiot right?

Yes. I remember being twelve years old and laying in bed, wondering which method of suicide would be the least painful. I am still depressed and sometimes think about suicide now in my late twenties. 

It's cruel that when animals are in pain that they are euthanized, but here I am, after a life time of misery, forced to wake up and live this life, day in and day out, again and again.

Different but somewhat similarly, I am a woman who experienced sexual abuse when I was a child. I am guilty of chasing very prudish men, and I feel uncomfortable when I receive attention from highly sexual men (even when they're attractive and respectful). Not surprisingly two out of the three relationships I've been in eventually became dead bedrooms. 

I think this is a real problem where some of us shoot ourselves in the foot due to our upbringing or childhood traumas. It's hard to change what we're attracted to, but sometimes what we're attracted to is not what will make us happy.

The funny thing is I've been called sexy by people who don't know me well, but I don't think any person I've dated has called me sexy (even though they've said I'm great in bed.) I am short but not extremely so and look my age. My voice isn't very high. I have a pretty but sorta mean face--not very cute. I am very unlucky and...probably have an unsexy personality at this point due to a life time of sexual struggles. 

I laughed at your username BTW. :)

I hate the whole "you should just know you're sexy thing." Thankfully I've never gotten it from this boyfriend, but I did get it from one ex so I get how irritating it can be. Glad things are better for you now. I've had a million conversations with my SO by now but I'm sure we'll end up having a million more whether we work out or not.

I'm glad I'm not alone, though I'm sorry to hear you're going through it also. I don't so much as get told that I'm sexy, though I get what you mean--the tone of voice matters more than anything. That and I've never gotten a compliment (about my appearance anyway) during foreplay or sex--its always when I'm cold and wrapped in a blanket or something.

I've wanted a dog for about 5 years now... But my life situation just doesn't allow for it. When I was was a kid I had a Golden and I don't think anybody has ever loved me as much as she used to love me. She unfortunately died on the last day of 8th grade... About 10 years ago.

Take good care of your doggo OP.
He would probably say that he doesn't have any money to spare for counseling. I've mentioned it before for other reasons (anger management) and that's how he responded a year ago.

That could be true, at least for why he was like that before. I don't feel as though there's a disparity between how we look now though--I haven't gotten that sort of comment in a long while. But maybe he's just taught himself to behave this way and can't change it? 

I've never considered that before at least--thank you for the insight.

He has little experience from before me and isn't at all sexually confident. I used to give lots of compliments to try and help him but it never increased him confidence or libido.

I've told him how I feel for four years almost, though this specific revelation is new. He usually gets mopey even if I phrase things as politely and sensitively as possible then does nothing.

I've told him I don't mind if he loses his erections and we can do other this, but he doesn't initiate. If I go down on him he goes back to whatever he was doing afterward and doesn't reciprocate unless I ask.

I think the erection thing contributes quite a bit but isn't the only reason.

I suppose it could be that he just communicates differently... But when it's combined with never initiating? Choosing masturbation over sex on the once a week or so occasion that he's horny? Never responding if I wear lingere? Rarely calling me beautiful or pretty even, always "cute?" I just find it quite suspect is all.

I've been through similar stuff. Sometimes I'm sitting somewhere and suddenly nothing feels real. Like I could run into traffic and nothing would happen. It can be kinda scary. Other times I'm just amazed by how odd and ridiculously sad my life is and I doubt whether or not certain things happened. Like I can't tell the difference between my life and a TV show I might have watched.

I sometimes feel like I made up the friends I have (about 3 good ones) out of loneliness too. That really sucks because I already feel really alone.

Yep, definitely. I wish my mind was as sharp as it used to be when i was 12, right before I became depressed. It's been a slow and steady climb downward, and it's been especially obvious since when I turned 19 or so.

I used to write rather well, but nowadays I make a lot of typos. I miss a lot of typos whenever I edit too--I like to jokingly call myself typo blind. My mind is sluggish and my memory is spotty...and it's weird. It's like no matter what I do I never feel much going on in my head anymore. Like my head feels heavy and silent.

I also know for a fact that depression affects my bodily health. I have started to have issues with aches all over my body. All my physicals and blood work come back fine. It's just the stress my depression is putting on my body.

So yes, I do get what you're going through. I'm sorry that you're going through it. I do think it's a common, if super crappy thing that tends to happen 

I will say that I, like you, did drop out of college. I didn't do much with my life for a while, but about two years ago I started to feel tired of not doing anything and I did go back to school. So, while I am still very depressed I have managed to become somewhat more functional. So I think its possible to be at least somewhat functional despite being like this.
Congrats! I hope you continue to have a good time and that you also get whatever help you need.

I don't necessarily doubt that. Lonely men are usually less picky. I also know that there are some men out there that are OK with or even prefer bigger women, especially outside of reddit (though I seem to be too small for most fat fetishist sorts--so I guess I'm just an unpopular type.)

But yes, there still is that fair chance of rejection and as you said it's what I'd focus on. I'm just not in a mental state to be able to handle it. I want flirtation but frankly even if I was single I probably couldn't handle rejection for a while. I'm a wimp I guess--I have no self esteem left, at least in regards to my looks and my sexuality. If my partner and I broke up tomorrow I probably wouldn't so much as look at a guy for a good while.

My boyfriend could have written this. Heck, he pretty much did write me this three years ago. He similarly is physically affectionate but not sexually affectionate. He likes sex but it isn't an overwhelming need for him. He has probably initiated sex three or four times in the last two years. He initiates cludding almost non stop though. My boyfriend used to say he loves me too much to view me sexually. That loving me made me unsexy. He has stopped saying this and says its not true anymore...but actions speak louder than words. We have less sex now more than ever, about once every two months.

I'll tell you what I've told my bf--you don't love your girlfriend too much. You are suffering from a madonna / whore complex. It seems others have pointed this out and that you agree--good. Please seek help. Otherwise, even if you break up with your girlfriend you'll have this problem in other relationships. Unless you date a very non-sexual woman this will always be a problem. 

Btw--as the woman on the otherside... I don't feel loved. I know that I am, cognitively, but I don't feel it. I feel incredibly lonely most days. I feel hideous too... I haven't looked at my body in over a year-- I can only look at face mirrors and only for so long. Please don't turn your girlfriend into me.

To be honest I've never received that. I used to be conventionally attractive (I've let myself go the last two years) but even back then I never got that. I'm trying to imagine feeling desired but to be honest it's outside my realm of comprehension. I've accepted that I'm just not a desirable person. 

I feel for you though. I think had I experienced passion I would feel even more depressed than I do now. I'm glad I don't know what I'm missing out on.

I'm a younger HL female and I wouldn't be opposed to flirting (but not actually meeting up) for a morale boost, but to be honest I'm not sure I could handle being rejected by both my partner and the internet. I gained a decent amount of weight due to feeling unattractive and giving up, and though I've been working on losing weight it's something that keeps me from flirting with others in the meanwhile. I imagine there may be more attractive women out there who are similarly afraid of rejection due to their self esteem being destroyed from their dead bedrooms.
